key_insight: Selected machine-learning models outperformed average multilayer perceptron accuracy in five of six COVID-19 outcome-prediction tasks, but performance varied widely.
clinical_relevance: The study explores prediction of death, ICU admission, and improvement or worsening in hospitalized COVID-19 patients, without establishing readiness for clinical use.
method: Compared five classifiers: logistic regression, KNN, CART, Naive Bayes, and SVM.
Tested ANOVA, mutual information, and recursive feature elimination; selecting 20 features generally improved cross-validated accuracy.
Compared selected ML models with multilayer perceptrons using one to five hidden layers.
evidence_signal: Two cohorts from Algeria (80 patients) and France (99 patients) were evaluated using 30 repetitions of five-fold training cross-validation and separate hold-out testing; selected ML test accuracies ranged from 0.47 to 0.95.
watch_item: Small cohorts and variable accuracy limit confidence; larger, independent validation is needed before clinical use.
paper_title: Application of Machine Learning and Deep Learning in diagnosis Covid19
